key_insight: Removing cognitive biases from LLM outputs does not always improve their decision-making; some biases are contextually functional and can support effective choices rather than being purely errors.
problem_solved: Challenges the assumption that debiasing LLMs uniformly improves performance by investigating the relationship between measured cognitive biases and practical decision-making outcomes.
method: Quantify cognitive biases expressed by multiple LLMs across controlled decision-making tasks and scenarios.
Apply debiasing interventions or prompts and compare downstream decision quality using task-relevant performance metrics.
Analyze trade-offs and context dependence to identify when bias reduction helps or harms decisions.
impact: Encourages practitioners to evaluate debiasing efforts against decision-quality metrics and context-specific goals rather than bias metrics alone. Promotes nuanced model auditing and task-aware mitigation strategies for safer, more effective deployments.
visual_elements: Scatter plot: bias-score (x) vs decision-quality (y) showing cases where lower bias does not imply higher decision quality.
Pipeline diagram: bias measurement → debiasing intervention → decision task evaluation to illustrate the experimental workflow.
Heatmap or matrix: tasks × models showing where debiasing improves, harms, or has no effect on decisions.
Trade-off icon/scale: simple infographic depicting 'bias reduction' on one side and 'decision effectiveness' on the other to convey trade-offs.
paper_title: LLMs displaying less cognitive bias are not necessarily better decision makers
paper_authors: Vittoria Dentella, Marco Marelli, Luca Rinaldi
